newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's anti-kidnap czar says he's resigning.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's anti-kidnap czar says he's resigning.

text.p: Colombian "anti-kidnapping czar" Alberto Villamizar announced plans to step down on Wednesday and said he may be appointed the country's ambassador to Cuba.
"My involvement in the anti-kidnapping programme is coming to an end," Villamizar told the Radionet radio news programme. "I'll be leaving this position soon."
Villamizar, a former lawmaker and ambassador, was appointed head of President Ernesto Samper's newly created anti-kidnapping office in 1995.

He did not say why he was leaving the post. But he noted that it was extremely "stressful" since Colombia -- where more than 1,400 were abducted last year -- has one of the world's highest kidnapping rates.

The kidnapping of Villamizar's wife and sister in 1990 prompted Nobel laureate Gabriel Garcia Marquez, an old friend of his, to treat the subject in his latest book, a non-fiction account of a string of high-profile abductions carried out by Colombian drug lords as part of their fight against their extradition to the United States.
In the radio interview, Villamizar confirmed reports that he may be named ambassador to Havana but stressed that nothing definite had been decided about his future yet.
"If Cuba comes through it would be to continue my work in the area of humanising the war," he said.

He did not elaborate, but his comment was widely interpreted to mean that he would seek to use the embassy in Havana as a site for possible peace talks with Colombia's leading leftist guerrilla groups.
